tooltip_room_range_modes: Cuts room-mode resonances and leaves the bass balance as it is; the safest choice.
tooltip_room_range_schroeder: Makes the response flat up to the Schroeder frequency, including dips a real room EQ cannot fill.
tooltip_room_mode_eq: Corrects the frequency response at each ear position; the timing of the bass stays as recorded.
tooltip_room_mode_tuning: Applies to each speaker the correction a room-correction processor would have made during the recording: a detailed frequency response correction in the low frequencies, a broad tone correction above them, speaker levels and timing. Both ears get the same correction. Uses the room measurements at the ear positions; room.wav is not used. The output starts later by the tuning delay.
tooltip_room_mode_tuning2: Applies to each speaker the room correction of SECS 2 (Speaker Gallery): a PEQ and an FIR in front of the speaker that correct its bass response and, within the filter's latency, part of the room's bass timing. Speaker levels are matched to the quietest one. Both ears get the same correction. Uses the room measurements at the ear positions; room.wav is not used. The output starts later by the filter's latency.

room_file_summary_rew: {count} measurements with an impulse response, {rate} Hz
room_file_microphone_calibrated: Microphone: {name}. The project includes its calibration, which is used when no Mic Calibration file is set.
room_file_skipped: No impulse response, so it cannot be used
room_file_subwoofer: Subwoofer. The BRIR has no subwoofer channel, so it is used only if you pick a speaker for it.

brir_file_one_position: This project has only one measured position. A BRIR needs the two ears measured at two positions.

label_headphone_file_right: Right earcup at the right ear:

headphone_file_same: Both earcups use the same measurement. Choose a different one for each.
hint_headphone_file: The folder's headphones.wav is not read.
studio_disclosure_headphone_comp_desc: Correct using a measurement of the headphone response
cli_brir_measurement_file_replaces_folde: The folder's {count} speaker recordings are not used because a BRIR measurement file is set
cli_brir_measurement_file_itd: Time difference between the ears per speaker (ms, right minus left) {list}
cli_brir_measurement_file_itd_large: {speaker}: the ears are {ms} ms apart, more than a head allows. The two ears may have been measured with different delays.
cli_brir_measurement_file_itd_zero: Every side speaker reaches both ears at the same moment. If the ears were measured separately without a timing reference, the time difference between them is lost.
cli_headphone_measurement_file_replaces_: {file} in the folder is not used because a headphone measurement file is set
tooltip_room_tuning2_mode_zero: Corrects the frequency response with PEQ only. No latency is added and the timing of the bass stays as recorded.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mode_mixed: PEQ and an FIR with 8 ms latency. The FIR corrects part of the room's bass timing within that latency.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mode_linear: PEQ and an FIR with 28 ms latency, which corrects more of the room's bass timing.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mode_long: PEQ and a long FIR with 200 ms latency, which corrects the most bass timing. Every channel starts 200 ms later.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mode_custom: PEQ and an FIR with the latency you enter (30–200 ms). A longer latency corrects more of the bass timing.
tooltip_room_tuning2_high: Auto multiplies the Schroeder frequency of the chosen basis by the reach, with a minimum of 100 Hz and a maximum of 500 Hz times the reach. Without a room volume or a Schroeder frequency it is 500 Hz.
tooltip_room_tuning2_level_match: Lowers every speaker to the level of the quietest one, as SECS 2 does. Turn it off to keep the levels as recorded.
checkbox_room_tuning2_mimo: Cancel late bass with the other speakers (MIMO)
tooltip_room_tuning2_mimo: Adds to each speaker low-frequency copies played by the other speakers, designed to cancel the bass that lingers at the ears after the first 60 ms (adjustable below). Works only below the upper limit, and a check keeps every band from getting worse.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mimo_early: How long after the direct sound the MIMO copies may start to act. A shorter time lets them also shorten the early bass decay, but drives them harder, so the check turns them down more often. 60 ms is the earlier behaviour.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mimo_ear_guard: The check that turns the MIMO copies down looks at both ears together, so a copy that helps one ear more than it hurts the other gets through. With this on, the copies are turned down whenever either ear gets worse. The README names the ear that set the limit.
tooltip_room_tuning2_dip_limit: A dip that falls below the response's one-octave envelope is filled by 2 dB plus half of the rest, 6 dB at most, instead of up to the boost limit. Narrow cancellations then take less boost; broad losses are still corrected in full. The limited dips are listed in the README.
tooltip_room_tuning2_low_protect: Finds where the speaker's own response rolls off (10 dB below its 200 to 1000 Hz level) and allows no boost below that frequency, with the boost limit ramping up over the octave above it. The PEQ bands and the FIR are checked afterwards so no boost leaks below the rolloff. Without a rolloff above 20 Hz nothing changes.
tooltip_room_tuning2_mode_decay: Finds room modes below 160 Hz that ring well past the room's 200 to 500 Hz decay and adds a cut at each, at most four, so the mode dies away sooner instead of only getting less boost. Works with every filter. The cuts are listed in the README.
checkbox_room_tuning2_lf_align: Align the bass arrival with the treble
tooltip_room_tuning2_lf_align: Below about 200 Hz the FIR moves each speaker's bass so it arrives with its treble; below the speaker's own rolloff the bass keeps that rolloff's delay. The bass is pulled forward by at most one and a half periods, which keeps the pre-ringing in check. The 8 ms filter usually cannot pull the full amount.
checkbox_room_tuning2_hf_phase: Match the treble phase above the band
tooltip_room_tuning2_hf_phase: Above the correction band the FIR leaves a fixed phase turn that differs from speaker to speaker. This undoes it over the three octaves above the band, only by adding delay there, so every speaker's treble keeps the same phase.
hint_room_tuning2_fir_only: PEQ only has no FIR, so the bass arrival and the treble phase stay as recorded.
tooltip_room_tuning2_high_basis: Strict uses the room decay at 500 Hz and 1 kHz. Lenient also measures the decay in third-octave bands from 100 to 500 Hz and takes the highest band whose own Schroeder estimate reaches it; it is never below the strict value. Treated rooms usually ring longer in the bass, so lenient goes higher there.
tooltip_room_tuning2_high_transition: Multiplies the Schroeder frequency to correct further into the transition region above it. ×2 allows up to 1 kHz and ×4 up to 2 kHz.
hint_room_tuning2_high_needs_volume: The basis and the reach need the room volume or a Schroeder frequency below. Without them the limit stays at 500 Hz.
tooltip_room_tuning2_input_hp: An 8th-order high-pass at this frequency on every speaker, 10 to 50 Hz, applied after the correction is designed. All speakers pass the same filter, so their phase relation above the cut stays the same while the deepest bass is not driven. Leave empty for none.
tooltip_room_tuning2_bands: Corrects up to four more ranges above the main band, written as low-high pairs in Hz and separated by commas, for example 1000-3000. Each range fades in over half an octave below its low edge and out over half an octave above its high edge. Leave empty for none.
hint_itd_mode_off: The time differences between the ears stay as recorded. The report after processing shows them for every speaker.
hint_itd_mode_symmetric: Mirror pairs (FL/FR, SL/SR…) get the same time difference and the center speakers none, which removes a head turned during the recording and a microphone sitting deeper in one ear.
hint_itd_mode_model: Every speaker gets the time difference of a spherical head at its nominal direction. Front speakers of real heads usually measure smaller than the model.
hint_head_radius: Empty: estimated from the side pair of the recording.
hint_itd_report: Positive values: the sound reaches the left ear first. Bass L−R below 120 Hz should be the same in both ears; what differs is the recording chain.
cli_itd_report: Interaural time differences: head turned {yaw}° to the left, centre offset {offset_us} µs, recording chain left minus right {balance} dB
cli_itd_pairing: Left/right balance of the final BRIR: speaker recording {speaker_db} dB, headphone recording {headphone_db} dB, predicted {predicted_db} dB
cli_itd_pairing_warning: The final BRIR will be {predicted_db} dB louder in the left ear than the right (speaker recording {speaker_db} dB, headphone recording {headphone_db} dB). The microphones were probably on different inputs in the two recordings. Record the headphones again with the same microphone on the same input, or set channel_balance.
cli_itd_head_turned: The head was turned about {yaw}° to the left during the speaker recording (mirror pairs are asymmetric). itd_mode=symmetric removes the asymmetry.
cli_itd_corrected: ITD correction ({mode}): {count} speakers adjusted, largest change {max_us} µs
cli_itd_skipped: {speaker}: ITD correction skipped, the change of {us} µs is too large
cli_readme_itd_row: {speaker}: measured {measured_us} µs, spherical head {model_us} µs, final {after_us} µs
cli_readme_itd_summary: Head turned {yaw}° to the left, centre offset {offset_us} µs, recording chain left minus right {balance} dB, head radius {radius_cm} cm.
cli_readme_itd_pairing: Final left/right balance: speaker recording {speaker_db} dB, headphone recording {headphone_db} dB, predicted {predicted_db} dB.
cli_room_tuning2: Virtual room tuning 2 from {low} to {high} Hz; every channel starts {delay} ms later
cli_room_tuning2_preecho: {speaker}: pre-echo reaches {db} dB before the direct sound; a filter with less latency reduces it
cli_room_tuning2_mimo: {speaker}: {supports} other speakers cancel its late bass (MIMO), at {db} dB
cli_room_tuning2_mimo_off: {speaker}: MIMO would make a bass band worse, so this speaker gets no MIMO
cli_room_tuning2_mimo_ear_band: {speaker}: MIMO {scale} dB rejected at the {ear} ear; late energy in {lo}-{hi} Hz rose by {db} dB
cli_room_tuning2_mimo_ear_tail: {speaker}: MIMO {scale} dB rejected at the {ear} ear; tail energy at {freq} Hz rose by {db} dB
cli_room_tuning2_low_protect: {speaker}: low-end protection, rolloff (Hz): {rolloff}; {reduced} PEQ bands reduced, {cuts} protective cuts, limit satisfied: {limited}
cli_room_tuning2_dip_limit: {speaker}: boost limited in {count} dips; deepest at {hz} Hz, depth {depth} dB, allowed fill {fill} dB
cli_room_tuning2_bands: Virtual room tuning 2 correction bands: {bands} Hz
cli_room_tuning2_lf_align: {speaker}: bass arrival alignment from {f_lin} Hz, phase strength {strength}, bass arrival relative to treble {arrival} ms, advance limited: {limited}
cli_room_tuning2_mode_decay_none: {speaker}: mode-decay target {target} s; no cut needed
cli_room_tuning2_high: Virtual room tuning 2 automatic upper limit: basis {basis}, multiplier ×{factor}, Schroeder {schroeder} Hz, lenient band {band} Hz ({band_t60} s), upper limit {high} Hz
cli_room_tuning2_high_no_volume: Virtual room tuning 2 upper-limit basis and multiplier have no effect without a room volume or a Schroeder frequency; the upper limit remains 500 Hz.
cli_room_tuning2_input_hp: Virtual room tuning 2 common input high-pass: {freq} Hz
cli_room_tuning2_pair_phase: {a} + {b}, {ear} ear: when playing the same signal, the speakers partly cancel each other in these bass bands: {spans}
cli_room_tuning2_pair_phase_hint: Low-frequency arrival alignment can bring the speakers' bass phase closer.
cli_room_tuning2_hf_phase: {speaker}: treble phase rotation {rotation} degrees, phase correction limited: {limited}
cli_room_tuning2_hf_phase_none: {speaker}: treble phase correction skipped; range {low}-{high} Hz is less than one octave
tooltip_room_tuning_curtain: Above this frequency only a broad tone correction is applied; the detailed correction fades out over the next octave.
tooltip_room_tuning_level_match: Matches the speakers' levels at the listening position within ±6 dB, as a room-correction processor does. Turn it off to keep the levels as recorded.
checkbox_room_tuning_phase_schroeder: Correct timing only up to the Schroeder frequency
tooltip_room_tuning_phase_schroeder: Checked: only the room's bass timing up to the Schroeder frequency is corrected. Unchecked: timing is corrected over the full band, where the room measurements at both ear positions agree.
label_room_tuning_phase_current: Current setting: {limit}, chosen in the Studio layout
tooltip_room_tuning_phase_limit: Up to the Schroeder frequency, the room's bass timing is corrected. Higher limits also correct the speaker's own timing, for example around its crossover, where the room measurements at both ear positions agree. Off corrects the frequency response only and adds no delay.
cli_room_tuning: Virtual room tuning up to {freq} Hz; every channel starts {delay} ms later
cli_room_tuning_off: Virtual room tuning without timing correction: frequency response and speaker levels only, no delay added
cli_room_tuning_single_point: {speaker}: room measurement at one ear position only; it is used for the whole speaker
cli_room_tuning_room_wav_ignored: room.wav is not used by virtual room tuning; it uses the room measurements at the ear positions
cli_room_tuning_no_data: No speaker has room measurements at the ear positions, so virtual room tuning is not applied
cli_room_tuning_level_inconsistent: {speaker}: the room measurement level differs from the recording by {db} dB, so this speaker's level is not matched
cli_room_tuning_mismatch: {speaker}: the room measurements do not match this recording's left/right arrival order or listening position; check that they belong to this recording
cli_room_tuning_weak: {speaker}: the room measurements differ from the in-ear recording's bass response by {db} dB on average (30–300 Hz); they may not represent the ear positions
cli_room_tuning_preecho: {speaker}: pre-echo reaches {db} dB before the direct sound; a shorter tuning delay reduces it
tooltip_room_range_extreme: Corrects up to the Schroeder frequency and also applies a smoothed tone correction to the speaker and room up to 10 kHz; above about 400 Hz this is a broad tone adjustment, not an exact correction.
tooltip_room_range_legacy: The 2.x behaviour, and the only range that uses Specific Limit and Generic Limit.
tooltip_vbass_room_handoff: Room correction leaves everything below the crossover to virtual bass, except with the Legacy (2.x) range.
tooltip_vbass_mode_auto: Finds where the speakers lose bass and sets the crossover one octave above that frequency. If they do not lose bass, nothing is added.
tooltip_vbass_mode_manual: Uses the frequency below. Set above the speakers' limit, it replaces the measured bass up to that frequency with flat synthesized bass.
tooltip_vbass_mode_legacy: The 2.x method: the level is matched at the crossover frequency alone, without timing alignment or the room target.
cli_room_range: Room correction range: {range}, up to {f_hi} Hz
cli_room_schroeder: Schroeder frequency {freq} Hz (reverberation time {t60} s, room volume {volume} m³)
cli_room_schroeder_assumed: Schroeder frequency {freq} Hz (reverberation time {t60} s, room volume assumed to be 50 m³)
cli_room_schroeder_fallback: Could not measure the reverberation time; using a Schroeder frequency of {freq} Hz
cli_room_rolloff: {speaker} {side}: the speaker rolls off below {freq} Hz, so nothing is boosted there
cli_room_rolloff_snr: {speaker} {side}: the measurement is too noisy below {freq} Hz, so nothing is boosted there
cli_room_snr_unavailable: {speaker} {side}: the room measurement is shorter than one second, so boosts are not limited by its noise level
cli_room_selfcheck_warning: {speaker} {side}: {rms} dB RMS error remains between {lo} and {hi} Hz after room correction; check the room measurement
cli_room_vbass_handoff: Room correction leaves the range below {freq} Hz to virtual bass
cli_vbass_auto: Virtual bass crossover: {freq} Hz, found in the measurements ({speaker} loses bass below {rolloff} Hz)
cli_vbass_auto_none: No bass loss found in the measurements, so virtual bass was not applied. To apply it anyway, choose a manual crossover
cli_vbass_below_rolloff: {speaker} loses bass below about {rolloff} Hz, too close to the {freq} Hz crossover: the bass just above the crossover stays weak
cli_vbass_match: Virtual bass level matched to the response between {lo} and {hi} Hz; delayed {delay} ms to line up with the speakers at the crossover
cli_vbass_room_target: Virtual bass follows the bass shape of the room target
cli_warning_layout_partial: {layout}: {file} has silent tracks for channels that were not measured: {missing}
cli_info_layout_missing: {layout} needs {count} more speakers for its channel-order file: {missing}
cli_readme_layouts_note: Each channel has two tracks, left ear first, in the format’s channel order. LFE tracks are silent.
cli_readme_layouts_note_lfe_filled: Each channel has two tracks, left ear first, in the format’s channel order.
cli_readme_layouts_atmos_order: Dolby publishes no channel order above 9.1.6. Tracks 1–32 follow the 9.1.6 interchange order of Apple and AWS MediaConvert; the remaining tracks follow the order of the Dolby Atmos Home Theater Installation Guidelines. No decoder outputs this order.
cli_readme_layouts_dts_order: The order follows the 32-bit channel mask in ETSI TS 103 491 Table B-5. DTS publishes no PCM order for a 30.2 decoder.
cli_readme_layouts_atmos_916_order: The order is the 9.1.6 interchange order of Apple and AWS MediaConvert (L R C LFE Ls Rs Lrs Rrs Lw Rw Ltf Rtf Ltm Rtm Ltr Rtr).
cli_readme_layouts_atmos_subset_order: Dolby publishes no channel order for this layout. It follows the 9.1.6 interchange order of Apple and AWS MediaConvert without the channels the layout does not have.
cli_readme_layouts_partial: Channels that were not measured have silent tracks: {missing}
hint_channel_order: A Mac sends the channels of an HDMI or DisplayPort output in the receiver's order. If a sweep plays from the wrong speaker, compare the device channels with Configure Speakers in Audio MIDI Setup.
hint_channel_order_auto_hdmi: This output is HDMI or DisplayPort, so the HDMI order is used.
hint_channel_order_auto_standard: This output is not HDMI or DisplayPort, so the standard order is used. For an aggregate device whose first channels are an HDMI output, choose HDMI.
hint_sweep_layout_codes: The Speakers field already lists all the codes after the arrows. Remove any speaker you are not measuring. Format labels can name other positions: channel 1 of 22.2 (FL, 60°) is WL here.
button_sweep_use_layout: Use every speaker in this layout
label_layout_files_force: Formats to save even with speakers missing:
hint_layout_files: Missing speakers get silent tracks. Formats you leave unchecked are still saved when every speaker is measured.
option_layout_files_listed: Also the formats I pick, with speakers missing
hint_layout_files_auto: When every channel of a format was measured, the BRIR is saved again in that format's channel order (for example atmos_9.1.6.wav). Of 9.1, 9.1.4 and 9.1.6 only the largest is saved.
hint_layout_files_none: Only hrir.wav and hesuvi.wav are saved.
hint_missing_speakers: For hesuvi.wav, hrir.wav and the channel-order files. The nearest measured speaker on the same side and at the same height is copied, and a missing center speaker is made from the pair beside it. Height channels are never filled from ear-level speakers.
hint_lfe_mode_none: The LFE tracks of the channel-order files stay silent. hesuvi.wav and hrir.wav have no LFE track.
hint_lfe_mode_center: The LFE tracks use the center speaker, or the two front speakers when the center was not measured.
hint_lfe_mode_all: The LFE tracks are made from the bass of every measured speaker below 120 Hz. Averaging the directions evens out the peaks and dips of any one position, as several subwoofers do in a room.
hint_guided_intro: Measure more speaker positions than you have speakers: sit in a swivel chair and turn between recordings as each step shows. Every step is saved under the name Processing reads.
hint_guided_distance: Sit at least 1.5 m from the speakers; closer than that narrows the sound. Tape on the floor at each angle makes the turns repeatable.
option_guided_off: Off: every speaker stays in place
option_guided_mono: One speaker on the left output
guided_face_between: Face the point midway between the two speakers.
guided_turn_around: Turn around so the speakers are behind you.
guided_ear_speaker_left: Turn so your left ear points toward the speaker.
guided_ear_speaker_right: Turn so your right ear points toward the speaker.
guided_ear_left_speaker_left: Turn so your left ear points toward the left speaker.
guided_ear_left_speaker_right: Turn so your right ear points toward the left speaker.
guided_checks_ok: No problems found in this recording.
guided_all_done: Every step is recorded. Record the headphones next, then generate the BRIR in Processing.
guided_diagram_label: Top view of your head and the speakers for this step
guided_countdown: Recording starts in {seconds} s. Turn now and hold still.
record_check_no_signal: {speaker}: the microphones did not pick up the sweep (signal-to-noise {snr_db} dB). Check that the speaker is on and connected, then record again.
record_check_input_silent: The input recorded only digital silence. Check that the input device is the binaural microphone and that it is not muted.
record_check_input_silent_macos: The input recorded only digital silence. On macOS an app without microphone access receives only silence. Allow Impulcifer in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone, then quit and reopen Impulcifer and record again.
record_check_clipping: {speaker}: the recording clipped (peak {peak_db} dBFS). Lower the playback volume or the microphone gain, then record again.
record_check_quiet: {speaker}: the recording is very quiet (peak {peak_db} dBFS). Raise the playback volume or the microphone gain.
record_check_noisy: {speaker}: the room was noisy during this recording (signal-to-noise {snr_db} dB). Make the room quieter, then record again.
record_check_wrong_side_left: {speaker} should be on your left, but the sound reached your right ear first ({itd_us} µs). Check which way you turned, then record again.
record_check_wrong_side_right: {speaker} should be on your right, but the sound reached your left ear first ({itd_us} µs). Check which way you turned, then record again.
record_check_off_center: {speaker}: the sound reached one ear {itd_us} µs before the other, about {measured}° off center. Face the direction the step shows, then record again.
record_check_angle_too_far: {speaker}: the sound reached your ears {itd_us} µs apart, which matches about {measured}° instead of {expected}°. You turned too far; turn back a little and record again.
record_check_angle_too_little: {speaker}: the sound reached your ears {itd_us} µs apart, which matches about {measured}° instead of {expected}°. You did not turn far enough; turn a little further and record again.
record_check_angle_off: {speaker}: the sound reached your ears {itd_us} µs apart, which matches about {measured}° instead of {expected}°. Make sure your ear points toward the speaker, then record again.
record_check_ear_silent_left: {speaker}: your left microphone picked up {db_diff} dB less than the right one. Check that the left microphone is inserted and connected, then record again.
record_check_ear_silent_right: {speaker}: your right microphone picked up {db_diff} dB less than the left one. Check that the right microphone is inserted and connected, then record again.
record_check_polarity: {speaker}: one microphone's signal is inverted relative to the other. Check the microphone wiring or the interface's polarity setting, then record again.
record_check_mics_swapped: The left and right microphones look swapped: the speakers reached the wrong ear first. Swap the microphones or the input channels, then record again.
record_check_distortion: {speaker}: the speaker is distorting (harmonics at {distortion_db} dB). Lower the playback volume, then record again.
record_check_itd_mismatch: {speaker}: the time difference between your ears is {itd_us} µs, but {reference} at the same angle measured {reference_itd_us} µs ({diff_us} µs apart). One of them was turned differently; record the one that is off again.
record_check_input_balance: The left input is {db_diff} dB louder than the right below 120 Hz, where both ears should be equal. Set both input gains equal, or make sure the headphone recording uses the same microphone on the same input.
record_check_headphone_balance: Headphone recording: left minus right {db_diff} dB, while the speaker recordings of this folder differ by the opposite amount. The final BRIR would be {predicted_db} dB off between the ears. Check that each microphone is on the same input as during the speaker recording.
record_check_level_changed: {speaker}: the level differs by {db_diff} dB from the earlier steps. Keep the playback volume and your distance to the speakers the same, then record again.
